title: Uncertainty Regarding Volume and Quality Disclosers in Resource Reports: Impact on Mineral Asset Valuations
content: An officially authorized geological report is commonly required to legally recognize the existence of a mineral deposit. Among other functions, it constitutes the primary input for mineral asset valuation. As the resources and reserves disclosed are subject to estimates and characterized with a certain confidence level, valuators must include this factor in their calculations. Valuators are accustomed to ambiguity, but they need precise details to determine which information is subject to what level of uncertainty. Geological reports typically include information on the confidence level (sometimes in the form of the maximum error), but in most cases, it is one figure related to the volume. The study presented herein aims to verify whether such a narrow approach to geological risk is sufficient for mineral asset valuation. This research covers both actual documentation from Poland and a few other European countries and related scientific articles and was supported by a calculation model. This article demonstrates the importance of the physical and chemical factors of the minerals in determining the value of a mineral deposit, which often surpasses that of the volume. Unfortunately, although geological reports providing a confidence level of estimates refer to the volume, they often neglect to consider uncertainty in the evaluation of the physical and chemical factors. This deficiency will be mitigated by both professional standards and legal regulations.
